Q: What exercises improve problem-solving skills in programming? A:

I think both approaches are useful: solving algorithm problems and building small projects.

Another useful practice is to look at other people's solutions after solving a problem. This helps you learn different ways to think about the same problem and improve your own approach.

Q: MySQL comment syntax - What's the difference between "#" and "-- "? A:

Both Oracle and SQL Server (as well as DB2 and others) support the -- and /* */ (multi-line) comment standard. So it's a good habit to use the same style in MySQL, as you will probably encounter situations where you're programming in multiple environments.

The requirement for a space after -- is a MySQL oddity, but is hardly a big deal as it helps clarity.

If, of course, you are using a lot of perl and MySQL, then you may opt for the # comment for similar reasons...

Q: What is the correct way to comment in SQL? A:

Both of your examples are correct, and it is good practice of doing comments in an SQL script.

  • -- is used for single line comment.
  • /* */ is used for multiple line comments.

A comment is generally given before logic.

Something like:

/* Count the number of users */
Count(*) AS "NumberOfUsers"

Or a single-line comment can be given after an expression as follows for good readability:

Count(*) AS "NumberOfUsers" -- Count number of users

Q: Error in if, the condition has length > 1 A:

To answer your question directly, it means that if() received a vector with more than one value. Example:

vector= 1:2
if(vector>1.5) {print("big")} else{print("small")

From a logical point of view, it also makes sense. if() is meant to return a single TRUE or a single FALSE which will dictate what pieces of code get executed. But if you give two values it does not know what to do. Is (1,2) bigger or smaller than 1.5?

So to ask if a vector is greater or smaller than a number makes no sense.

But you hint at a similar operation that does make sense, ifelse(). This is an operation that is applying if for every element of vector.

result = ifelse(vector>1.5,"big","small")

is equivalent to:

result= character(2)
for(i in 1:length(vector) {
   if(vector[i]>1.5) {result[i]="big"} else{result[i]="small"}
}

Note that in this for loop we are running as many if() as there are elements in our vector and receiving as many results. So that is a different operation than if(vector>1.5) and a valid one.

Q: How to fix 'ORA-00932: inconsistent datatypes: expected - got CLOB' when used with GROUP BY clause? A: 
CREATE VIEW sample_description AS 
SELECT person_description, name, employee_id
  FROM employee_table 
 WHERE employee_id IN (SELECT employee_id OVER (PARTITION BY employee_id, NAME) 
                         FROM employee_table);
